title: Aft Pylon Fairing Heat Shield and Seal Renewal at the Auran 7700 Interface
abstract: Renewal of the aft pylon fairing heat shield and its interface seal on Auran-powered twin-engine aircraft, after thermal distortion of the original seal allowed hot gas recirculation into the fairing cavity.

sections.reason: Line reports of scorching on the inner face of the aft pylon fairing accumulated from 2016 onwards on Auran-powered aircraft, with thirty-four occurrences across a fleet of about 210. Thermal survey traced the cause to permanent set in the original interface seal after repeated exposure above its rated temperature during high-thrust take-offs in hot conditions. Once the seal has taken a set, the gap opens and exhaust gas recirculates into the fairing cavity, discolouring the fairing skin and, in four cases, degrading the adjacent drain line. The condition has no immediate airworthiness effect but drives repeat unscheduled fairing removal.
sections.description: The pylon fairing skin panel D5450133608027 is retained and a new formed heat shield is installed on its inner face, standing off the skin by 8 mm to create a ventilated air gap. The upper fairing doubler JAR270491-60 is replaced by an item with the standoff bosses machined in, and the lower fairing lug kit ROD165267-21 is re-worked so that the fairing can be closed on the thicker seal without preloading the latch. Countersunk screws EN962457-4D retain the shield and washers AES161398-12 are used under each head. Clevis pins EN169671-8B at the fairing hinge are replaced as a matter of course because they are disturbed. Access is from below through the pylon fairing itself in zones 431, 433 and 441, with the engine installed. Revised detail is on drawing D54501398265.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 5.7 kg per aircraft pair. No electrical load change. The new fairing is interchangeable with the original at aircraft level, but the doubler and the lug kit must be changed as a set. The unscheduled fairing removal rate is expected to fall from 0.16 to below 0.02 per aircraft per year. No dispatch or MMEL effect. The AMM fairing opening and closing task requires a revised torque sequence because the seal is thicker.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN S01466 in November 2020. Retrofit through Service Bulletin SLN-54-1013 at any line maintenance opportunity where the fairing can be opened; typical elapsed time is fourteen hours per pylon and the engine does not need to be removed.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric about the centre line; no reportable effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN S01466, pylon dressing sequence unchanged
